title: 2008 AMC 12B Problem 17
statement: Let \(A,\) \(B\) and \(C\) be three distinct points on the graph of \(y = x^2\) such that line \(AB\) is parallel to the \(x\)-axis and \(\triangle ABC\) is a right triangle with area \(2008.\) What is the sum of the digits of the \(y\)-coordinate of \(C?\)

solutions.text:
Since \(AB\) is horizontal, take \(A = (a, a^2)\) and \(B = (-a, a^2),\) and let \(C = (c, c^2).\) The right angle cannot be at \(A\) or \(B\) (that would need \(c = \pm a\)), so it is at \(C.\)

Put \(d = a^2-c^2.\) Taking the dot product of \(\overrightarrow{CA}\) and \(\overrightarrow{CB}\) gives \(d(d-1)=0.\) The points are distinct, so \(d \ne 0;\) hence \(a^2-c^2=1.\) This value is the height of the triangle above \(\overline{AB}.\)

The area is \(\tfrac12 \cdot AB \cdot \text{height}\) \(= \tfrac12 (2|a|)(1)\) \(= |a| = 2008,\) so \(a^2 = 2008^2 = 4{,}032{,}064\) and the \(y\)-coordinate of \(C\) is \(c^2 = a^2 - 1 = 4{,}032{,}063.\)

Its digit sum is \(4 + 0 + 3 + 2 + 0 + 6 + 3 = 18.\)

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: Write \(A = (a, a^2)\) and \(B = (-a, a^2);\) since \(A, B, C\) have distinct \(x\)-coordinates, the right angle is at \(C\)
Perpendicular legs \(CA\) and \(CB\) force \(a^2 - c^2 = 1,\) the height above \(\overline{AB};\) get \(|a|\) from the area, then \(c^2\)
